chapter_theme: One song at Vagaimanagar (வாகைமாநகர்): the poet's infatuation with women's speech, eyes, breasts and gait, set against Murugan's own love for the hunter girl, whose hair he combed and whose feet he held.

990.reading: The poet lists the women's speech sweet as cane juice, eyes deadly as Death's poison, calling voices, heavy breasts, ear-ornaments, elephant gait and slender waist, and asks whether, in infatuation, he will wander in the bitterness and the moisture of the sinful body. The praise tells how Murugan gave the hunter girl surpassing love, took on the hunter's guise, then on the platform in the field combed her hair, held her feet, drank the nectar of her mouth and embraced her to end her longing, at Vagaimanagar of groves.
990.nuance: The two halves use the same words: the poet wanders in மயல் and in the ஊறல் of the body, while Murugan drinks the ஊறல் of Valli's mouth so that her மயல் ends. The god's love is told as tenderly and physically as the poet's sin, and the song leaves the contrast unstated.
